$comment: P69 (lane lm, D-LINK-OBJECT-READERS-DROP-INTERIOR-SYMBOL-OFFSET): a DSS STATIC LIBRARY whose code addresses its own interior — a dense 12-case switch (a jump table: one abs64 slot per case, each naming a block label inside the function) and a computed goto (block addresses taken by the code) — linked into a program by --resolve-library on all five pairs, so every reference crosses the pair's relocatable-object READER. DSS's COFF and Mach-O writers name each such block with an interior label (class STATIC type 0 / N_ALT_ENTRY), and the two readers kept the label as the relocation target, which no atom owns and the linker's compound index never declares: ✔MEASURED before the fix, pe64 and macho64-arm64 refused the link with K_SymbolUndefined once per jump-table slot (12) while elf64-x86_64, whose reader already rebound a body-less section-defined target to its containing atom, linked and ran. Now all three readers rebind through one shared rule (link/format/section_relative_target.hpp). The sums are arithmetic: lib_switch over k = -1..12 is 100+...+111 plus two defaults of -1 = 1264; lib_computed_goto over k = 0..5 is 7+8+9+7+8+9 = 48.
